record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.context_brief: Plank coverage of a unit ball
record.original_question: In d-dimensional Euclidean space E^d, a plank is a closed region bounded by two parallel hyperplanes, and its width is the distance between those boundary hyperplanes. Given a family of planks whose total width is smaller than 2, what is the maximum possible volume of the subset of the unit ball in E^d that is covered by the planks?

evidence.quote: A plank is a closed region of the d-dimensional Euclidean space Ed bounded by a pair of parallel hyperplanes. The width of a plank is the distance between its boundary hyperplanes. Question 2. Given a family of planks whose sum of widths is smaller than 2, what is the maximum volume of the part of the unit ball in Ed that can be covered by the planks?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $d \geq 2$ and let $E^d$ denote $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. A plank in $E^d$ is a closed region bounded by two parallel hyperplanes, and the width of a plank is the (perpendicular) distance between its two bounding hyperplanes. Let $B^d \subset E^d$ denote the closed unit ball. Consider an arbitrary finite (or countable) family $\{P_i\}$ of planks in $E^d$ with $\sum_i w(P_i) < 2$, where $w(P_i)$ is the width of $P_i$. Determine the supremum, over all such families and all positions of the planks, of the $d$-dimensional Lebesgue measure of $B^d \cap \bigcup_i P_i$. Equivalently, find a sharp upper bound (as a function of $d$ and of $\sum_i w(P_i)$) on the volume of the part of the unit ball that can be covered by such a family of planks.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2022 survey on plank theorems indicates that determining the maximum volume of the part of the unit ball in E^d coverable by a family of planks of total width less than 2 remains an open problem. Standard plank theorems (Bang, Ball) give that the full ball cannot be covered when the total width is less than 2 (in fact, ≤ 2 for the diameter case), but the precise extremal volume question is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Plank theorems and their applications: a survey (Verreault, 2022)
status_evidence.snippet: The maximum volume of the unit ball in E^d covered by planks of total width less than 2 is still an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is reported as open in a recent survey of plank theorems.

status_evidence.title: Packing and Covering (G. Fejes Tóth, Handbook of Discrete and Comp. Geom.)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Tarski/Bang plank theorems and related open questions on covering balls by planks.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references list plank-covering extremal problems among unresolved questions.
